note: build with LAZYOS_DESKTOP=1 LAZYOS_XUI_AUTOSTART=term LAZYOS_UI_PROBE=1 LAZYOS_LABEL_TRACE=1 LAZYOS_RESET_OS=1; docs/devtool-packages-plan.md 'T-later: Terminal': the Terminal is the package os.lazy.terminal, a developer tool that is the user's shell, so what runs in it acts as the session's owner
init stamps the label and reads it back from the kernel
pkgd answers a caller under the Terminal's label as the session's owner (it refuses every other labelled caller)
the source rule of pkgd (only /transient, /system/share and the home folder) applies to the Terminal exactly as to the unlabelled user it replaced
the administrator prompt works from the Terminal, and names the asker as a developer tool
a developer-tool install is asked for by the Installer only: refused before any prompt
init starts a built-in program for the Terminal: the label is not handed down to an unlabelled program, as it was refused for any labelled caller
the Devices window took the focus: back to the Terminal's left edge, which it does not cover

a shell tool is not denied the credential services (the Playground is): keyd itself refuses a caller that is not accountsd (EPERM), the same answer the unlabelled Terminal got, and the kernel prints no LABEL:DENY for it
init accepts powerctl from the Terminal, as it accepted it from the unlabelled one
